AUDIO TRANSCRIPT
ERA II
Municipal Utility Engineer
Station Seven seal schedule revised again. Manufacturer specification was one hundred eighty days. We reduced it to ninety. Then forty-five. New directive says inspect every eleven days.
Eleven. We have six hundred pumps in this district. There physically are not enough maintenance crews. PolyCore insists the new material line will fix it. Maybe.
For now we're stripping good seals from nonessential equipment to keep drinking water moving. Central administration asked whether this qualifies as an emergency.
I told them the pumps are running. They said then technically it doesn't. Fine. Ask me again when they aren't.

AUDIO TRANSCRIPT
ERA V
Dr. Sora Kel
People ask when civilization collapsed. They expect a date, a bomb, a blackout—something dramatic. Look at this station. It still works. Mostly.

Three crews spend every waking hour cannibalizing the other four stations around it. The grid works because substations are stripped for parts. Hospitals work because closed wards keep open wards alive.
Trains run because two dead locomotives keep one moving. We are not maintaining infrastructure anymore. We are consuming infrastructure to preserve the appearance that the system still exists.
No organism has to destroy civilization overnight. It only has to make civilization cost more to maintain than civilization can produce.
